result.topic_en: Riemann rewrites the hydrodynamic equations of the rotating fluid ellipsoid in a moving coordinate system: he projects the accelerations onto the moving axes, introduces the angular velocities p, q, r, and expresses the relative velocities and accelerations through the axis rates of change and the rotation rates.

methods.what: Equations of motion projected onto the moving axes (gravitational potential and pressure)
Velocity components along the moving axes
Orthogonality relations of the direction cosines, used to define the angular velocities p, q, r
Absolute velocity in the rotating frame = relative velocity plus a rotation term
Acceleration components in the rotating frame
Rotation of the scaled coordinates with angular velocities p1, q1, r1 (second frame)
Velocity field linear in the coordinates, with the axis rates of change and the rotation rates as coefficients

items.english: The task is now to bring the equations into a form in which their derivatives with respect to the quantities ξ, η, ζ can be substituted, for which some preparations are still necessary.

items.quote: Was die geometrische Bedeutung dieser Grössen betrifft, so sind, wie leicht ersichtlich, $\xi', \eta', \zeta'$ die Geschwindigkeitscoordinaten
items.english: As regards the geometric meaning of these quantities, ξ', η', ζ' are, as is easily seen, the velocity coordinates (with respect to the ξ, η, ζ coordinate system).
